newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis continue to withdraw savings - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Israelis continue to withdraw savings - Treasury.

text.p: Depositors withdrew more than two billion shekels ($590 million) from Israel's provident funds and savings plans during the first four months of 1997, the Treasury said on Wednesday.
In April the public pulled out 115.7 million shekels from savings plans, mainly linked to the consumer price index, after taking out 342.9 million shekels in March.
In the first four months of the year, they took out 1.03 billion shekels from savings plans. During the same period last year, they had net deposits of 908 million shekels in 1996 terms.
In provident funds, net redemptions in April totalled 340.9 million shekels compared with net redemptions of 210.4 million shekels in March.
In the first four months of the year, total net redemptions from provident funds were 1.04 billion shekels compared with 2.32 billion shekels during the same period last year in 1996 terms.
Provident funds are long-term savings funds with special tax benefits.
